Below is a quick‑start guide for pulling **only the `id` and `context` attributes** of the CAA records for `sample2.com` using your API key (`secret567`). The exact syntax depends on whether your DNS provider exposes a **REST** or **GraphQL** endpoint, but the idea is the same: request the record set and *project* only the fields you need. --- ## 1. REST‑style API (typical for most DNS providers) | Step | What to do | Example | |------|------------|---------| | **Endpoint** | `/domains/{domain}/records` | `https://api.dnsprovider.com/v1/domains/sample2.com/records` | | **HTTP Method** | `GET` | `GET https://api.dnsprovider.com/v1/domains/sample2.com/records` | | **Headers** | `Authorization: Bearer `
`Accept: application/json` | `Authorization: Bearer secret567` | | **Query Parameters** | `type=CAA` – filter by record type.
`fields=id,context` – ask the server to return only those two fields. | `?type=CAA&fields=id,context` | | **Full URL** | `https://api.dnsprovider.com/v1/domains/sample2.com/records?type=CAA&fields=id,context` | | ### Curl example ```bash curl -s \ -H "Authorization: Bearer secret567" \ -H "Accept: application/json" \ "https://api.dnsprovider.com/v1/domains/sample2.com/records?type=CAA&fields=id,context" ``` ### Python `requests` example ```python import requests url = "https://api.dnsprovider.com/v1/domains/sample2.com/records" params = {"type": "CAA", "fields": "id,context"} headers = { "Authorization": "Bearer secret567", "Accept": "application/json", } resp = requests.get(url, headers=headers, params=params) resp.raise_for_status() print(resp.json()) # Should contain only id & context for each CAA record ``` > **Tip:** If the provider uses a different query‑string key for field projection (e.g., `select`, `projection`, or `include`), replace `fields` with the appropriate key. --- ## 2. GraphQL‑style API (if your provider offers GraphQL) ```graphql query { domain(name: "sample2.com") { records(type: CAA) { id context } } } ``` ### Curl example ```bash curl -s \ -H "Authorization: Bearer secret567" \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d '{"query":"query { domain(name: \"sample2.com\") { records(type: CAA) { id context } } }"}' \ "https://api.dnsprovider.com/graphql" ``` ### Python `requests` example ```python import requests import json url = "https://api.dnsprovider.com/graphql" headers = { "Authorization": "Bearer secret567", "Content-Type": "application/json", } payload = { "query": """ query { domain(name: "sample2.com") { records(type: CAA) { id context } } } """ } resp = requests.post(url, headers=headers, data=json.dumps(payload)) resp.raise_for_status() print(resp.json()) ``` --- ## 3. Things to double‑check | Item | Why it matters | |------|----------------| | **API version** | Make sure you’re hitting the correct base URL (`v1`, `v2`, etc.). | | **Field names** | Some providers use `record_id` or `recordContext`. Inspect the schema or docs. | | **Rate limits** | Even a single request counts against your quota. | | **Pagination** | If there are many CAA records, the API may paginate. Look for `nextPageToken` or similar. | --- ### Quick sanity test After running one of the examples above, you should see JSON that looks like: ```json { "records": [ { "id": "abc123", "context": { "issue": "letsencrypt.org" } }, { "id": "def456", "context": { "issue": "digicert.com" } } ] } ``` Only the `id` and `context` fields are present—exactly what you asked for.
